# ai

> Model-pinned ZCode harness kit plus cross-harness skill categories. No
> installer, no build step, no dependencies: an AI agent pointed at this
> repo installs it by following the procedures below.

Layout: the ZCode kit under `harness/zcode/`; other top-level directories
except `research/` and `archive/` (`copy/`, `coding/`, `i18n/`,
`languages/rust/`, `product/`, `testing/`, `web-spec/`) are cross-harness
skill categories. To install, follow [install.md](install.md), which
enforces a strict **Global Core vs Per-Project Niche** split:
- **Global Core (`~/.zcode/` and `~/.agents/skills/`)**: only the 4 core
  agents (`general-pro`, `general-flash`, `explore-flash`,
  `workflow-launcher`), the 2 core ZCode skills (`z-workflow`,
  `z-project-init`), and the 5 universal baseline skills
  (`antislop-copy`, `code-comments`, `test-quality-guardrails`,
  `test-quality-tdd-agents`, `test-quality-audit`).
- **Per-Project Niche (`<project>/.zcode/` and `<project>/.agents/skills/`, via `z-project-init`)**:
  niche `z-*` specialist agents and stack-specific domain skills
  (`languages/rust/rust-*`, `product/*`, `testing/*`, and external
  framework skills) install only into the project that uses them and
  record their `hmziqrs/ai` commit SHA and file hashes in
  `<project>/.zcode/hmziqrs-ai-snapshot.json`.
Agent definitions must be regular files — ZCode's discovery silently skips
symlinks; `find ~/.zcode/agents -type l` and
`find <project>/.zcode/agents -type l` printing nothing confirms none.

`research/` and `archive/` are excluded from installation and routine
exploration. Read them only when the user explicitly requests that
material or the task is maintenance of it. Follow the hard rule in
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

## ZCode kit (`harness/zcode/`)

- [harness/zcode/agents/general-flash.md](harness/zcode/agents/general-flash.md): full-tools general agent pinned to glm-5.3-flash — objectively checkable work (CRUD, boilerplate, mechanical verification).
- [harness/zcode/agents/explore-flash.md](harness/zcode/agents/explore-flash.md): read-only search + code-audit agent pinned to glm-5.3-flash — reports findings, no verdict authority.
- [harness/zcode/agents/general-pro.md](harness/zcode/agents/general-pro.md): full-tools judgment agent pinned to glm-5.3 — complex implementation, audit verdicts, continue/stop decisions.
- [harness/zcode/agents/workflow-launcher.md](harness/zcode/agents/workflow-launcher.md): full-access Flash HIGH launcher for z-workflow — does everything pre-workflow (explores, bootstraps an uninitialized project, parses optional phases and round budgets from the brief, plans every area), then writes one fresh dynamic-workflows script where each area runs its own phase chain with zero global barriers, and launches it with CreateWorkflow.
- [harness/zcode/skills/z-workflow/SKILL.md](harness/zcode/skills/z-workflow/SKILL.md): the only workflow skill — parallel by default with zero global phase barriers. Every task is its own area running its own chain (implement → optional audit → optional test → …) inside its own fan-out callback, so an area advances the moment its own work lands. Optional verification phases run only when the brief names them (default 1 round, explicit N, or until-zero-issues) and attach per area — vision/browser only to UI-producing areas, native testing only to device-targeting areas; per-area checks stay scoped to the area's own files; whole-tree gates run once at the final join. Areas carry niche personas distilled from matching z-* specialists; model pins are per subagent inside the script (implementers default GLM-5.3-Flash at HIGH, main-tier GLM-5.3 only on request, vision interpreters always Flash — the only vision-capable model), so one workflow mixes models across areas and phases. Testing phases use the matching capture tooling — agent-browser (web), open-computer-use (desktop), mobilecli (mobile), tui-use (TUI) — with z-qa-evaluator / z-native-device-verifier personas; shared devices serialize through one FIFO device-operator subagent. No git worktrees, branches or commits — areas edit the current checkout directly. Fresh script per task, nothing saved, live per-area board. references/proven-patterns.md catalogues ten campaign-verified mixed-model workflow shapes the launcher plans from.
- [harness/zcode/skills/z-project-init/SKILL.md](harness/zcode/skills/z-project-init/SKILL.md): per-project ZCode initializer and snapshot manager — inspects project manifests, installs only the required niche `z-*` sub-agents and domain skills, and writes `.zcode/hmziqrs-ai-snapshot.json` for drift detection and isolated per-project updates while keeping the core agents global.

The ZCode kit also supplies reusable `z-*` domain and verification
personas, including `z-qa-evaluator` (skeptical browser QA against
acceptance criteria) and `z-security-auditor` (read-only diff security
audit). Agent descriptions select expertise; the coordinator assigns
scope and explicit analysis, implementation, or review authority.

## Cross-harness skill categories

Every top-level directory except `harness/`, `research/`, and `archive/`
is a category holding plain-SKILL.md skills (no harness tooling).
Category skills install for every harness; research and archive never
install.

- [copy/antislop-copy/SKILL.md](copy/antislop-copy/SKILL.md): cuts consumer-facing website copy to the shortest version that still answers the visitor's questions, without inventing or bending facts.
- [coding/code-comments/SKILL.md](coding/code-comments/SKILL.md): hard comment discipline for agent-written code — use whenever writing or editing code in any language, even when the request never mentions comments. Zero comments by default; names, types, structure, and tests carry the meaning. Only public-API contract docs, convention-required SAFETY blocks, and link-carrying last-resort constraint notes survive, never longer than 2 lines (3 absolute max). Bans narration, section banners, change-log and AI-voice comments.
- [coding/test-quality-guardrails/SKILL.md](coding/test-quality-guardrails/SKILL.md): stop AI agents from generating bloated, low-value unit tests — rules-file policies with copy-paste CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.cursorrules blocks: default-off test generation, read-only failing tests (never modify or delete a failing test to make it pass), targeted runs in the agent loop with the full suite in CI/hooks, and when tests are worth explicitly asking for.
- [coding/test-quality-tdd-agents/SKILL.md](coding/test-quality-tdd-agents/SKILL.md): tests-first workflows for AI coding agents — the confirm-fail red-green loop with tests frozen during implementation, humans writing or reviewing the tests as the spec, characterization tests for legacy code, and property-based testing as the better agent assignment than hand-written example tests.
- [coding/test-quality-audit/SKILL.md](coding/test-quality-audit/SKILL.md): audit and prune AI-written test suites — mutation testing as the quality gate, coverage as a vanity metric, implementation-coupling and mirroring smells, the "not too many, mostly integration" mix, risk-based coverage allocation, and a promote/flag/delete triage runbook.
- [i18n/rust-i18n/SKILL.md](i18n/rust-i18n/SKILL.md): Longbridge `rust-i18n` reference for Rust/GPUI desktop localization — `i18n!`/`t!`, YAML/JSON/TOML locale files, runtime `set_locale`, `gpui_component` string overrides via `rust_i18n::extend!`, and `cargo i18n` extraction.
- [i18n/sveltekit-paraglide/SKILL.md](i18n/sveltekit-paraglide/SKILL.md): Paraglide JS v2 for SvelteKit — Vite plugin, `messages/<locale>.json`, `m.*` runtime, `paraglideMiddleware` and reroute hooks, locale strategies, and SSR/prerender pitfalls.
- [i18n/flutter-slang/SKILL.md](i18n/flutter-slang/SKILL.md): slang v4 for Flutter — `slang.yaml`/`build.yaml`, typed JSON sources, `context.t`, `LocaleSettings` switching and persistence, drift checks, with the official gen-l10n/ARB alternative.
- [i18n/astro-i18n/SKILL.md](i18n/astro-i18n/SKILL.md): Astro built-in i18n routing — `i18n` config, `astro:i18n` helpers, per-locale content collections, the UI-string dictionary recipe, and when to add Paraglide JS.
- [languages/rust/rust-superopt/SKILL.md](languages/rust/rust-superopt/SKILL.md): entry point for "make this Rust faster" — benchmarks-first triage across compute vs memory vs lock vs IO, release-profile hygiene, measurement discipline, and codegen-inspection/PGO/BOLT tooling; routes to the sibling rust skills.
- [languages/rust/rust-simd-crates/SKILL.md](languages/rust/rust-simd-crates/SKILL.md): adopt an existing SIMD-accelerated crate (JSON, hashing, compression, UTF-8 validation, base64/hex, CRC, FFT/BLAS, crypto, image codecs, search) instead of hand-writing kernels — selection, runtime-vs-compile-time dispatch caveats, feature-flag swaps, serde_json → simd-json/sonic-rs migration.
- [languages/rust/rust-simd-kernels/SKILL.md](languages/rust/rust-simd-kernels/SKILL.md): hand-written SIMD/vector kernels when crates and the autovectorizer are not enough — std::simd / core::simd / wide / pulp, C-intrinsic ports, `#[target_feature]` and runtime dispatch, codegen verification with cargo-show-asm / llvm-mca / LLVM remarks.
- [languages/rust/rust-parallel-cache/SKILL.md](languages/rust/rust-parallel-cache/SKILL.md): parallel and cache-friendly Rust — rayon pool configuration, work-stealing vs pinned-shard design, false-sharing measurement and padding, cache tiling, NUMA first-touch, Apple Silicon QoS/E-core steering.
- [languages/rust/rust-fast-architecture/SKILL.md](languages/rust/rust-fast-architecture/SKILL.md): architecture-level speed for whole Rust services — contention math, single-writer actors, lock downgrade at commit, write-behind group commit, adaptive linger, pooling, deterministic simulation testing, async-runtime chooser (glommio/monoio/compio/tokio).
- [product/prd-authoring/SKILL.md](product/prd-authoring/SKILL.md): staged pipeline for writing or amending a PRD that agents build from — levels, stable IDs, Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, lint and critic gates.
- [product/site-recon/SKILL.md](product/site-recon/SKILL.md): read-only reconnaissance of a public reference website into a discovery pack — archetypes, captures, data model, journeys, gated-area assumptions, parity spec.
- [testing/parity-testing/SKILL.md](testing/parity-testing/SKILL.md): reference-parity tests for a website clone — aria-snapshot structure matching, masked pixel diffs of static chrome, journey replay, per-archetype parity scores, noise and sensitivity calibration.
